light: This is one ordinary frame pulled from a normal handheld home video shot by her grandson with a consumer camera at eye level, simply recording what happens, not composing a photo. The framing is casual and a little off: something is cut by the edge of the frame. Almost everything in the frame is in focus, nothing blurred out: the cluttered kitchen background stays fully readable. The only light is what the place really has, and each person and object gets light according to where it stands; correctly exposed, the side near the window a little brighter and cooler, the far corners dimmer. Colours of an ordinary video with automatic white balance and almost no correction: moderate contrast, soft highlights, mild sensor noise and light compression, faint motion blur on anything moving. Skin with pores, age spots and uneven tone; hair with stray strands; clothes and apron with real creases and flour dust. People are caught mid-action, unposed. Daylight from the window on the left plus the ceiling lamp.
look: Ordinary handheld home video filmed by her grandson with a consumer camera at eye level, small natural shakes and casual slightly imperfect framing, everything in the kitchen in focus, only the light the place really has, correctly exposed, automatic white balance, mild sensor noise; real skin and natural old hands; she moves naturally and unposed, nothing staged; no music.

clips.text: Now the eggs go in one at a time, and here's the first thing nobody tells you. You stir them in, you do not beat them. You don't want air in this pie.
clips.action: She cracks the egg into the bowl and stirs it in gently with the wooden spoon while she explains to her grandson. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: If you whip it, it puffs up in the oven like a souffle and then it falls and cracks down the middle. Stir, honey. Just stir.
clips.action: She keeps stirring gently, then lifts the wooden spoon and wags it at the camera, amused. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: You pour it into the crust, and it goes into a three hundred and fifty degree
clips.action: She pours the filling into the crust and scrapes the bowl with the spatula. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: Then ice water, three or four tablespoons, a spoon at a time, just until it holds together when you squeeze it.
clips.action: She spoons ice water onto the dough a little at a time, then squeezes a handful to show it holds. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: And now watch this, because this is Mrs. Lindqvist's trick. You put the dry mix right into the pie shell, and you pour the cream over it, and you stir it right there in the crust, gently, with your finger.
clips.action: She pours the cream into the pie shell and stirs it gently with her finger, laughing. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: No beater, no whisk. You don't want foam. The old Indiana ladies all did it this way, and she said if your finger's clean enough for the Lord, it's clean enough for the pie.
clips.action: She finishes stirring with her finger and holds it up to the camera, joking. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: Now carrying it to the oven is the hard part, because it's runny as milk. You go slow.
clips.action: She carries the runny pie very carefully to the oven and slides it in. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: Like this. Just rub it and let it fall. Rub it and let it fall. My hands aren't what they used to be, but they still remember this part.
clips.action: She rubs the butter into the flour and sugar with her fingertips and lets the crumbs fall. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: And here's Esther's trick. You dissolve the soda in the hot water first, see, it fizzes up, and then you stir that into the molasses and egg.
clips.action: She stirs the soda into the hot water, it fizzes, then she pours it into the molasses and stirs. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: You melt the butter in the skillet till it foams and starts to smell nutty, and then you stir in the brown sugar and you let it cook.
clips.action: She stirs the foaming butter in the iron skillet and tips in the brown sugar. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: And here's the trick. You take it darker than you think. When you're scared it's going to burn, give it one more minute. That's where the flavor is.
clips.action: She keeps stirring the darkening syrup, then raises the spoon and an eyebrow at the camera. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: Pour it in slow. It'll hiss at you. Keep stirring and it all melts back together into a beautiful brown milk.
clips.action: She pours the warm milk into the skillet, it hisses and steams, and she keeps stirring. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: Then you take a little of that hot mixture and you stir it into your beaten yolks, so they warm up slow and don't scramble.
clips.action: She spoons hot mixture into the yolks and whisks them. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: You beat the whites till they foam, then you add the sugar a spoon at a time, and you keep beating until it stands up in stiff shiny peaks.
clips.action: She beats the whites with the hand mixer until they stand in stiff shiny peaks, then lifts the beaters. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: And you push the meringue all the way out until it touches the crust all the way around. Seal it, like a lid. That's what stops it from weeping and from shrinking away from the
clips.action: She pushes the meringue out to the crust edge all the way around and pulls up peaks. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: Now the trick with this one is the raisins. You put them in a little pan, cover them with water, and simmer them five minutes. Then drain them.
clips.action: She pours the raisins into the simmering water, then drains them at the sink. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: Plump them first. They come out soft and juicy, like they just remembered they were grapes.
clips.action: She shakes the sieve and shows a spoonful of plump raisins to the camera. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: You don't crush the crackers. You break them with your hands, into big pieces, about like quarters. Like apple slices.
clips.action: She breaks the crackers by hand into big pieces into the crust and shows one piece. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: And here's the real secret. The part I never showed anybody. Mama let the syrup cool. All the way.
clips.action: She tests the cooling syrup with her fingertip at the window, telling the secret. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: Danny, taste that. Go on. Tell them what it is. See? Apples. He knows it's crackers, and he still says apples.
clips.action: She watches her grandson's hand take a bite of the pie and laughs at him. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.
